question.text: The Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty began construction of this waterway, which connects the Pacific and Atlantic Ocean through its namesake country.
question.clue: The building of this structure was made possible by Walter Reed's work controlling Yellow Fever.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous campaign slogans.
swap.text: This 28th U.S. President first elected in 1912 ran on the slogan "he kept us out of war" to win reelection in 1916. Ironically, this man entered the war after the sinking of the Lusitania.
swap.clue: This president sent 10,000 men under the command of John J. Pershing to Mexico to respond to border raids.

question.leadin: As President, this man authorized naval action that led to Panamanian independence and, eventually, the Panama Canal.
question.text: Name this US President, whose foreign policy is often referred to as "Big Stick" diplomacy and who went on an African safari shortly after leaving office.
question.clue: In his greatest office, he directed the Great White Fleet of the U.S. Navy to make a two-year circumnavigation of the globe.

swap.leadin: In 1920, this man ran for US President from a prison cell after being arrested for sedition.
swap.text: Name this politician who, with "Big Bill" Haywood, helped found the Industrial Workers of the World.
swap.clue: While participating in the ARU, this man was arrested for interfering with the mail, and was later represented by Clarence Darrow.

question.text: Early in her career, Perkins was appointed Head of the Committee on Public Safety that investigated this industrial fire. Locked stairways caused the deaths of 146 garment workers in this fire.
question.answerHtml: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire [accept synonyms for fire or synonyms of tragedy; accept the Triangle Shirtwaist Company Fire; or Triangle Waist Company Fire; prompt on answers mentioning Shirtwaist but not Triangle] Note to players: description NOT acceptable, specific term required
question.clue: Josephine Goldmark and Rose Schneiderman used this event as motivation to continue pressing for better working conditions, and it was investigated by future Labor secretary Frances Perkins.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about failed legislative initiatives in American history.
swap.text: This policy codified by the 18th Amendment and the Volstead Act banned the production and sale of alcoholic beverages. This policy was reversed with the ratification of the 21st Amendment in 1933.
swap.clue: Wayne Wheeler drafted a bill that would enforce this policy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about "Robber Baron" industrialists.
question.text: J.P. Morgan and other industrialists helped save the economy during this economic panic, which saw the collapse of the Knickerbocker Trust Company.
question.clue: This crisis occurred after an attempt by Otto and Augustus Heinze to corner the United Copper Company.

swap.text: The Blackstone Hotel in Chicago contained a "smoke-filled room" which nominated this man who promised a "return to normalcy." His Interior Secretary Albert Fall got in trouble for distributing leases in Elk Hills.
swap.clue: During his administration, the Nine Power Treaty was signed, reaffirming the earlier Open Door Policy for China.

question.leadin: Name these Chief Justices of the Supreme Court from some decisions they wrote.
question.text: Schecter Poultry v. U.S., Ashwander v. Tennessee Valley Authority, Norris v. Alabama
question.clue: He replaced Bainbridge Colby as Secretary of State and chaired the Washington Naval Conference.

swap.text: Early in his administration, Taft passed this tariff named for two Republican senators. It split Republicans into Progressive and Old Guard factions, leading to their loss in the elections of 1810.
swap.clue: This law was later modified by the Underwood Act, and this law included a provision allowing for free trade with the Philippines.

question.text: This co-founder of the IWW had been a leader of the Western Federation of Miners and an urn with half of his ashes in it was buried in the Kremlin upon his 1928 death.
question.clue: The Lawrence strike caused a split in the Socialist Party between Victor Berger's moderate faction and the radical militant faction led by this man, who later emigrated to the Soviet Union.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about West Coast Hotel Co. v. Parrish.
swap.text: The case ended an informal period in Supreme Court history started by this case. During this case's so-called "era," the Supreme Court struck down laws that regulated working conditions.
swap.clue: The argument that the Fourteenth Amendment does not "enact" Spencer's Social Statics was put forth in Holmes's dissent.

question.text: The greatest project of the Sui dynasty was a project of this type designed to connect northern and southern China by water. Jimmy Carter signed over a US-owned project of this type to Omar Torrijos in 1979.
question.clue: Yellow fever afflicted workers who built one of these structures across the Isthmus of Darien.

swap.leadin: When asked whether he was aware that the literacy tests he wanted were discriminatory, this man responded "Discrimination! Why that is exactly what we propose."
swap.text: Name this supporter of segregation who represented Virginia in both the Senate and the House. He was one of the two namesakes of a Banking Reform Act that created the FDIC.
swap.clue: In his sole Cabinet post he was appointed to replace William McAdoo and his most notable achievement in that office was the floating of a five billion dollar Victory Loan to liquidate World War I expenses.

question.text: Carrie Chapman Catt, the founder of this American organization, encouraged the Icelandic suffragette movement by enlisting Briet Bjarnheðinsdottir ("BREE-yet bjarn-HAY-theens-DOH-teer"). The NAWSA was succeeded by this organization that sponsored the U.S. presidential debates between 1976 and 1984.
question.clue: After winning the right to vote, NAWSA was reconstituted as this advocacy group. Prior to 1988, this group organized U.S. presidential debates.

swap.leadin: This company was accidentally sabotaged by "Joybubbles," a 7-year-old with perfect pitch; that feat was replicated by John Draper using Captain Crunch pirate whistles.
swap.text: Name this company that signed the Kingsbury Commitment to avoid one antitrust suit, but faced another in 1982. This company was purchased by its former subsidiary SBC in 2005.

question.text: Having already led the expedition to capture Pancho Villa in 1915, this commander of the Allied Expeditionary Force led it to Europe in 1917.
question.clue: The convoy inspired the Bureau of Public Roads to request an early model of a highway system, depicted in a map named for this man. West Point cadets coined this general's nickname based on his command of the 10th Cavalry Regiment of "Buffalo Soldiers."

swap.leadin: In 1919, this man purchased an auditorium in Harlem and named it Liberty Hall.
swap.text: Identify this black nationalist who established the Universal Negro Improvement Association and organized the formation of the Black Star shipping line, as part of his Back-to-Africa movement.
swap.clue: This man was imprisoned for five years for mail fraud after purchasing the SS Yarmouth as head of the Universal Negro Improvement Association.

question.text: This awesome jew, who would later Replace Holmes on the Supreme Court, wrote the opinion in Pfalsgraf. He also wrote a notable concurrence to Schechter Poultry and the book Paradoxes of Legal Science.
question.clue: After eighteen years of revolutionizing many areas of the common law from the New York Court of Appeals, this man was appointed to the Supreme Court by Herbert Hoover.

swap.leadin: This woman once organized a march of around 500 juvenile textile workers to the summer home of Teddy Roosevelt to protest child labor which was dubbed the Children's Crusade.
swap.text: Identify this "Angel of the Miners" who lends her name to a progressive magazine that leaked Mitt Romney's 47% Speech.
swap.clue: To protest the use of child labor in Pennsylvania silk mills, this activist marched young mill workers 120 miles to the house of Teddy Roosevelt.
